Reference

Dressmaker Wiki

This is the reference layer for the dressmaker game — the tables to keep open in a second tab. Dressmaker is a cozy dressmaking simulation from elyaradine, sarandipityx and raithza, published by Free Lives and out on Steam since September 21, 2026 for Windows and macOS.

Reviewed September 21, 2026

  • Fabric familiesCotton, linen, wool, silk, velvet
  • Launch content450+ fabrics, 150+ dress pieces
  • Accessories350+ across buttons, bows, appliqué, lace
  • AssemblyPattern pieces arranged on cloth by hand
  • DecorationPlaced freely after sewing
  • Not publishedPer-bolt stats, prices, unlock order

This wiki is the reference layer for the dressmaker game — fabric families, the pattern pieces a dress is built from, the four decoration types, the six-stage making loop and a plain-English glossary. Numbers the developers have not published are marked unpublished, not guessed.

How to use this wiki

What this page covers, and what it does not.

  • What is documented

    Fabric families, pattern pieces, decoration types, the order of the making loop and the vocabulary. Every line traces to an official source.

  • What is not documented

    Per-bolt stats, prices, unlock order and the full attribute list. If a number is missing here, the developers have not published it.

  • How to correct it

    Found something wrong or out of date? Tell us with the page and the source. Corrections come from official material only.

Fabric families at a glance

The store page names five fabrics — cotton, linen, wool, silk and velvet — inside a launch range of over 450. No per-bolt stats are published, so this table describes behaviour instead.

FabricWhat it does wellBest suited toWatch out for
CottonSoft drape, matte finish, holds a shapeEveryday commissions, fitted bodicesCreases; flat beside silk; hides buttons
LinenCool, dry handle, visible weaveSummer dresses, relaxed skirtsThe loud weave swallows fine lace; creases
WoolWarm, matte, structuredCold weather, tailored bodicesBulk at seams and hems; swallows light trims
SilkHigh shine, fluid drape, near-weightlessEvening and wedding commissionsOff-centre panels show in the light; slippery
VelvetDeep colour, light-absorbing pileOne statement piece, such as a bodicePile runs a direction; opposing panels read differently
Specialty and printedEverything else on the shelfPrints and print-led dressesNo per-bolt stats or unlock order published

Tip

the last row is a family, not a bolt. We can tell you how cotton behaves, not that bolt 217 runs heavy.

Pattern pieces and garment panels

A dress is assembled from pattern pieces you arrange, cut and sew: 'how you choose to arrange and cut out your fabric is what appears on the final dress.'

Tip

grain is the direction the threads run; align a piece with it and the panel hangs straight. Bias cuts diagonally across it for a softer drape.

Garment areaWhat it decidesWhat to consider
BodiceThe panel closest to the customer's face, and the busiestFine prints survive; align the centre front to the grain
SleevesA mirrored pair, cut twice as oppositesDirectional prints flip on the second sleeve
SkirtThe largest pieces, so the most cloth and print on showThe home for a statement fabric; bias is dramatic
Trim and finishingBands, edgings and decoration on the finished garmentJudge a trim against its panel — lace over velvet disappears

The how to play Dressmaker walkthrough takes these stages in order; sewing tips goes deeper on layout and seam order.

Decoration types

Four types — buttons, bows, appliqué and lace trims — placed 'wherever you like with complete creative freedom', from over 350 accessories. Appliqué is planned in the sketchbook, so it is a design choice too.

DecorationWhat it is forWhere it reads best
ButtonsSmall, repeated, precise — a row is rhythmCentre fronts, cuffs and bodice openings
BowsOne soft shape that pulls the eye to a pointWaistlines, shoulders, the back, a neckline
AppliquéShaped fabric placed on the surfaceMotifs on a skirt, or across a bodice
Lace trimEdging for borders, hems and seamsAny line worth following: a hem, a cuff, a panel edge

The making loop, in reference form

Six stages, in the order the game asks for them. Dressmaker runs on two currencies, coin and reputation.

StageWhat you doWhat it costs
1. Design in the sketchbookChoose silhouette, colour, samples and appliquéTime only — designing is planning, not spending
2. Buy fabricBuy from the shelves; over 450 fabrics shipCoin; per-fabric prices are not published
3. Arrange and cutLay the pieces out, check the mannequin, then cutThe cloth. Irreversible; the preview is the only undo.
4. Sew the panelsFeed the fabric through the sewing machineNothing — the machine has an infinite bobbin
5. DecorateAdd buttons, bows, appliqué, lace and accessoriesNot published; we will not guess
6. Hand in, or sell off the rackTurn the dress in, or sell pre-made dressesNothing up front — coin and reputation come back here

Handing in earns coin and reputation. What reputation unlocks, and in what order, has not been published. The customer preferences page covers reading the brief.

Key terms

The words the game uses in its interface, in plain English.

TermPlain-English meaning
GrainThe direction the threads run in a woven fabric; the predictable cut.
BiasCutting diagonally across the grain, for a softer drape.
PanelOne piece of a garment — bodice, sleeve, skirt, trim. You choose its fabric.
AppliquéShaped fabric stitched onto another as a design.
Off the rackReady-made rather than made to measure.
MannequinThe display figure that previews a garment before you cut.
NotionsSmall sewing supplies: buttons, trims, thread.

What this wiki is, and what it is not

This is a fan-made reference, not an official one. Every claim traces back to the official Steam store page or the developers' own itch.io devlog.

Note

in-game numbers are not published. Prices, unlock order, per-fabric stats and accessory costs have never been released, so any wiki quoting an exact coin price is guessing.

Something wrong or out of date? Tell us. To start playing instead, read how to play Dressmaker, then the sewing tips and system requirements.
